nodes.name: GET Agent Prompt (prospector)
nodes.notes: Same Render cold-start failure class as GET /sequences/due in Agent 6 -- retryOnFail rides it out instead of aborting the whole run before any searching even starts.

nodes.name: GET ICP Profile
nodes.notes: Same Render cold-start failure class as GET /sequences/due in Agent 6 -- retryOnFail rides it out instead of aborting the whole run before any searching even starts.

nodes.name: Tavily: Web Search
nodes.notes: Grounds the LLM in real search results instead of asking it to answer from training data. Requires the TAVILY_API_KEY n8n Variable (free tier: 1,000 searches/month, no card - https://tavily.com). Unlike Serper (Google's raw operator syntax), Tavily accepts plain natural-language queries with no site:/OR/parentheses restrictions. Build Search Query fans this out to up to 10 parallel per-item calls (one per job title) -- retryOnFail + onError:continueRegularOutput means one query's transient failure (network blip, momentary rate limit) degrades to that one query contributing zero results (Enrich Search Results already defaults a missing `results` field to []) instead of the default onError=stopWorkflow aborting the ENTIRE run and discarding the other 9 queries' results too.

nodes.name: Enrich Search Results
nodes.notes: Runs once per query batch (n8n's default per-item execution for Code nodes given N separate input items) and adds an extractedCompany field per result: for LinkedIn profile URLs it's parsed deterministically from the page header (name/company/location lines); for any other result (company team/leadership/about pages, press releases) it's guessed from the page title via a few common patterns ("X - Leadership", "Leadership - X", "Name - Title | X", "X - Team"). This gives the model the same kind of reliable anchor for non-LinkedIn sources that fixed the original 0-candidates issue for LinkedIn ones. IMPORTANT: this must use $input.all().map(...) and return one output item per input item -- a Code node's default "Run Once for All Items" mode makes bare $json silently resolve to just the FIRST input item, which is exactly the bug that made only 1 of up to 10 query batches ever reach the LLM despite Tavily correctly running all of them (verified live: a full 10-batch run took ~90s vs ~15-20s for the single-batch bug).

nodes.name: Call LLM (Web Search)
nodes.notes: Runs once PER job-title query batch (not once over every batch combined) -- an earlier version combined all batches' results into one call and hit a 54,795-token prompt that the model silently gave up on (a 9-token empty {"candidates":[]} response), verified via real execution data. Each batch's own ~20 results keeps the prompt to a few thousand tokens, well within the model's effective range.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((() => { const m = $('GET Agent Prompt (prospector)').first().json.agent.model; const model = (!m || /nemotron|openrouter/i.test(m)) ? 'gemini-3.5-flash-lite' : m; const body = { model, max_tokens: 8192, messages: [{role:'system', content: $('GET Agent Prompt (prospector)').first().json.agent.systemPrompt}, {role:'user', content: JSON.stringify({ icp: $('GET ICP Profile').first().json.icpProfile, searchQuery: $json.query, searchResults: $json.results })}] }; return body; })()) }}

nodes.name: Parse Candidates JSON
nodes.notes: OpenRouter/OpenAI-style response: the model's answer is a plain string at choices[0].message.content (no block array like Anthropic's format). Like Enrich Search Results, this must use $input.all().map(...) and return one item per batch -- bare $input.first() silently drops every batch after the first in a Code node's default "Run Once for All Items" mode.

nodes.name: Merge Query Batches
nodes.notes: Combines every job-title query batch's candidates back into one deduped list (by sourceUrl+name+company) before the existing single-report pipeline (IF: Has Candidates To Enrich onward, unchanged). One batch's LLM/parse failure never fails the whole run -- only surfaces as a run-level failure if every single batch failed AND none found candidates.

nodes.name: Normalize Split Candidate
nodes.notes: Split Out (previous node) nests each split element under its original field name (candidates) instead of flattening it, so { firstName, company, ... } arrives here as { candidates: { firstName, company, ... } }. That silently broke IF: Has Company (checking a field that no longer existed at top level) and corrupted the final payload sent to the app (422 Required). This unwraps it back to a flat candidate object. IMPORTANT: this must use $input.all().map(...) -- a Code node's default "Run Once for All Items" mode makes bare $json silently resolve to just the FIRST input item, which is exactly the bug that made every discovery run report exactly 1 lead created regardless of how many real candidates Split Out Candidates actually produced (verified live: execution 753 confirmed 7 candidates surviving end to end after this fix, vs 1 before).

nodes.name: Hunter: Email Finder
nodes.notes: Finds a real, verified email for a candidate by company + name. Requires the HUNTER_API_KEY n8n Variable (https://hunter.io) — free tier gives 25 searches/month. Only called when the candidate has a company name, since Hunter requires company or domain to search against.

nodes.name: Apply Hunter Result
nodes.notes: Only accepts Hunter's email if its own confidence score is >=50 - never fabricates or lowers the bar below what Hunter itself considers reliable. IMPORTANT: this must use $input.all().map(...), paired by index against $('IF: Has Company').all() -- like Normalize Split Candidate, the previous version's bare $input.item/$('IF: Has Company').item had no explicit "Run Once for Each Item" mode set, carrying the same only-processes-item-0 risk. Fixed pre-emptively alongside the confirmed Normalize Split Candidate bug.

nodes.name: POST /icp-profiles/:id/runs/:runId/results
nodes.notes: Same Render cold-start failure class as GET /sequences/due in Agent 6 -- without retryOnFail, hitting a cold app here after all the search/extraction work already succeeded would leave the LeadDiscoveryRun stuck forever with real candidates that never got reported.
